affectedPublicSurfaces: NO HTTP surface changes at all — no route, no request or response model, no field. The blast radius is entirely inside `services/agent/runner/`: `tool_executor.py` today dispatches with a literal if/elif over three module-level dicts imported at the top of the file — `PRODUCT_READ_TOOL_HANDLERS` (`tools/product.py`), `PRODUCT_WRITE_TOOL_HANDLERS` (`tools/product_write.py`) and `TERMINAL_TOOL_HANDLERS` (`tools/terminal.py`) — and the class is `ProductToolExecutor`. That is the only thing this slice reshapes.

The TOOL CONTEXT, which is the real change and is wider than the issue's bullet suggests. `ProductToolExecutor.__init__` takes `product_id: str` as CONSTRUCTOR STATE — deliberately never read from the model's params (its docstring says so) — and threads it into `ProductToolContext(product_id=self._product_id, ...)` at every dispatch. A non-product tool has no context object to receive; generalising the context to carry the RUN's subject (`subject_type`/`subject_ref` from #1701) plus the guarded resources is the substance of the slice, and the product domain must be migrated onto it with zero behaviour change.

`ToolSpec` (`services/agent/tools/registry.py`) — a frozen dataclass with `name`, `description`, `input_model`, `output_model`, `classification` (READ/WRITE), `policy` (AUTO/CONFIRM), `timeout_seconds` — gains a `domain` field, and registration of a domain-less spec is refused AT IMPORT TIME. `ToolRegistry` is explicit-registration with no decorators, so this is one additive frozen-dataclass field and one guard, not a framework.

The seam already exists and must be used, not replaced: `ToolExecutor` is a `@runtime_checkable Protocol` with the single method `execute(self, *, tool_name, params, tool_call_id=None) -> Mapping[str, Any]`. The domain handler registry (domain → handler table) sits behind that Protocol; the Protocol's own signature does NOT change, so `runner/core.py` and every existing caller keep compiling.

The CONFIRM pause is asserted to be DOMAIN-INDEPENDENT. Today the pause is driven by `ToolSpec.policy == CONFIRM` and lands in `waiting_approval` via `paused_for_confirmation`; a WRITE-CONFIRM tool registered in a test-only domain must pause identically, because ADR-075's consent binding is a property of the policy, never of the product domain. If it does not, the generalisation has leaked product assumptions into the consent path — the one thing this slice must not do.
NO schema change, no migration, nothing under apps/, packages/ or ios/.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. The dispatcher stays three literal handler dicts bound to `ProductToolContext(product_id=...)`, a non-product tool still has nowhere to live, and adding a WRITE tool still means five parallel edits named after products. That is the pre-existing state: nothing is exposed, nothing is partially applied, and no seller-visible behaviour changes.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Code-only rollback: redeploy the previous release and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker. There is NO schema to revert and NO downgrade to run — this slice owns no migration. Runs already completed keep their events and their `run_confirmations` rows, all written in the pre-existing shape because behaviour is unchanged by construction. A run SUSPENDED at CONFIRM across the rollback resumes correctly, because the consent binding is `params_sha` over the tool call's arguments and neither the arguments nor the hash function move in this slice — assert this explicitly pre-merge rather than assuming it. If #1701's schema must also be reverted, that downgrade is #1701's and must FAIL LOUDLY when any `workflow_runs` row carries a non-product subject or a NULL `product_id`, or when any run sits in `waiting_external`. Order: previous code first, any schema revert second.

doNotInfer: Do NOT read a migration number from head — do NOT write a migration at all. This slice has no schema change of any kind. The migration number and `down_revision` are RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue. NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename. The chain's single head today is `055_juli_app_sync_state_update` (revising `054_juli_app_bronze_select`), but W6 and W8 both hold unlanded numbers off-tree, and this tree already carries two same-numbered `043_*` files (`043_stop_reason_consent_pause` and `043_juli_app_role`, chained one after the other) from exactly this mistake.

ZERO behaviour change for `optimize_product_2` is the acceptance criterion, not an aspiration. The golden is `tests/fixtures/golden_scenarios/optimize_product_confirm_pause.json` (the tree's only golden scenario) and the prompt golden is `tests/fixtures/agent_prompt_gates/optimize_product_v3_composed.golden.md`. Do NOT regenerate either. If the golden moves, the migration was not behaviour-preserving and the diff is wrong — the golden is not.

Do NOT change the `ToolExecutor` Protocol's signature. `execute(self, *, tool_name, params, tool_call_id=None) -> Mapping[str, Any]` is the seam that already exists; widening it would push the change into `runner/core.py` and every caller, which is a different and much larger slice.

Do NOT let the model choose a domain, a subject or a product. `product_id` is constructor state on the executor precisely because it must never come from LLM input; the generalised context takes the subject from the RUN row (#1701's `subject_type`/`subject_ref`), never from `params`. A subject read out of a tool argument is a prompt-injection surface.

Do NOT derive the subject from revenue. `ProductsRepo.get_highest_revenue_product` has no place anywhere in the runner; #1702 removed it from approve and it must not reappear as a context fallback when a run's subject is not a product.

Do NOT make the CONFIRM policy domain-specific. Consent binding is ADR-075 and hangs off `ToolSpec.policy`; a per-domain confirm rule, a domain allow-list for pausing, or a domain that opts out of CONFIRM would fork the consent model.
Do NOT add a second reaper policy object or touch `workers/tasks/reaper.py`. Per-run policy resolution landed in #1702 through the existing `policy=` seam.

Do NOT delete the tool-registry contract test's capability→workflow assertion. Update it to know about domains — deleting a contract assertion because the shape moved is how a contract silently stops being one.

Do NOT emit or consume a per-order card, do NOT reuse the emission-budget suppression vocabulary (`active_cap`/`cooldown`/`weekly_novelty_cap`), and do NOT touch `services/action_cards/**` — cards are #1703's.

Do NOT register a real non-product tool here. The `inventory` domain in the acceptance criteria is TEST-ONLY; real tools land with their workflows in W9-B and W10. Registering one now ships a capability with no reviewed workflow behind it.

Do NOT open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051); do NOT touch apps/**, packages/** or ios/** — this epic's doNotLoad list. An executor that believes it needs a design reference here has been mis-routed: stop and report.

Bind every test collaborator to the REAL object's signature — the real `ToolRegistry`, the real `ToolSpec`, the real `WorkflowRunner`, the existing fake LLM adapter built on `LLMService.complete`. A `**kwargs` double proves routing, never that the real call would work.
